name: herdr
where_agents_run: your machine + saved SSH machines, in one window
checked_on: 2026-10-09 (latest release, herdr.dev agents, install and Windows docs)
source_note: Re-checked 2026-10-09 against the v0.9.3 release, herdr.dev's agents, install, connecting-machines and Windows pages, and its issue tracker. First checked 2026-09-28 against v0.9.1. Not installed or run here.

multi_provider_supervision.value: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, opencode, Grok and more

needs_you_signal.value: Each pane marked working, blocked, done or idle

approve_deny_prompt.value: Its CLI can type an answer; no allow or deny button

real_terminal.value: Every agent runs in its own real pane

session_organization.value: Workspaces and split panes; one list across machines

builtin_editors_browser.value: Runs your tools in panes; no editor or browser of its own

appearance_control.value: Your terminal's look; settings in its config file

worktree_management.value: Create, open and remove worktrees from the sidebar

planner_orchestrator.value: No planner; agents can start and prompt each other

agent_to_agent_messaging.value: Agents start, prompt and wait on each other

cross_provider_delegation.value: All agents in one list, local and remote

native_mobile_app.value: None; installer refuses Android, community Termux builds exist

phone_no_new_app.value: Any SSH app reattaches to the background server

remote_ssh.value: Saved SSH machines listed beside local ones

app_shell.value: Terminal UI: one Rust binary, no Electron

background_process.value: Yes: a background server keeps terminals running after you close the client or lose SSH

download_size.value: v0.9.3: 10 MB Windows zip, 22-24 MB macOS, 28-30 MB Linux

ram_vs_claude_desktop.value: Tiny (estimate: terminal app, one small Rust binary)

runs_in_terminal.value: Runs in whatever terminal you already use

license_cost.value: Apache-2.0, free, uses your own subscriptions

extensibility.value: Plugin marketplace plus a CLI and socket API

stability_maturity.value: v0.9.3, ~43k GitHub stars, fast-moving; Windows build is in beta
